claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr has improved plastic strain relative to pure tungsten at high temperature.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr has improved toughness relative to pure tungsten at high temperature.
The improved plastic strain and toughness are primarily caused by severe lattice distortion in the multi-principal-element solid solution.
Severe lattice distortion activates additional dislocation glide systems in WTaTiVZr.
Severe lattice distortion enhances dislocation mobility during deformation.
The initial WTaTiVZr material is an equimolar, homogeneous high-entropy alloy.
Temperatures of 800–1200 °C are representative of sustained plasma-facing-component service.
The applicable testing regime is one in which both materials remain microstructurally stable and undergo no secondary phase transformations.
Lattice distortion in WTaTiVZr promotes activation of a wider range of dislocation slip systems than in pure tungsten.
Lattice distortion in WTaTiVZr delays dislocation pile-up relative to pure tungsten.
Enhanced dislocation mobility and additional slip-system activation increase the alloy's capacity for plastic deformation.
Enhanced dislocation mobility and additional slip-system activation increase energy absorption before fracture.
Pure tungsten has limited slip activity relative to WTaTiVZr under the proposed conditions.
Under identical high-temperature loading, WTaTiVZr will have a higher strain to failure than pure tungsten.
Under identical high-temperature loading, WTaTiVZr will absorb more energy before fracture than pure tungsten.
Under identical high-temperature loading, WTaTiVZr will display more active dislocation motion than pure tungsten.
Pure tungsten is expected to have lower ductility and toughness because it has fewer operative slip systems and undergoes early dislocation pile-up.
The proposed mechanism may not apply when oxidation or significant phase changes occur.
Minor secondary-phase formation could influence the observed mechanical behavior.
Failure to observe additional slip-system activity or enhanced dislocation mobility in WTaTiVZr relative to tungsten would falsify the proposed mechanism.
